subject: Security gating — hosting path & artifact requests
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@medisure.com>, Ryan Patel <ryan.patel@medisure.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + immediate artifact asks (security gating)

Hi Aisha / Ryan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and three concrete asks so your security team can triage hosting options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem.

Key constraints you mentioned:
- Primary requirement: BAA-backed processing for PHI.
- SOC 2 Type II evidence requested for vendor evaluation; detail on control families and audit window helpful.
- Network controls: ability to restrict egress, customer-managed VPC peering, and private peering options.
- KMS/HSM integration for customer-owned keys and record of encryption-at-rest.
- Audit log retention window: 1 year, with export capability to your SIEM.

Recommendation (short):
- If you need full control + strict network isolation and on-prem access to keys: Private (VPC or on-prem) — higher setup time, but meets the strictest compliance ask.
- If you want Redwood-managed infra but isolated tenant and predictable throughput: Dedicated capacity + VPC peering + customer KMS is usually the fastest path to satisfy BAAs + SOC2 checks.
- Hosted API (public) is viable only when PHI handling is limited and legal signs off; otherwise we should avoid for this deployment.

Immediate asks for your Security team to review (can you share by Mon?):
1) Primary SOC 2 (Type II) report or bridge letter — we can provide ours; if you can share Medisure’s vendor intake SLA/threshold doc that helps.
2) Network diagram and list of allowed egress destinations (for Dedicated/VPC design).
3) Clarify whether Medisure requires customer-managed KMS (BYOK) or if an account-level HSM is acceptable.

I attached our latest SOC2 Type II and a BAA template we commonly use. I’ll also loop in our solutions engineer (Marissa) and infra lead (Karthik) to scope the Dedicated/VPC design once we get your network requirements.

Next steps I propose:
- A short 30-minute technical follow-up (Marissa + Karthik) to review network requirements and KMS approach — are you available Tue or Wed next week?
- You share the three artifacts above (SOC2/diagram/KMS requirement).

Thanks —
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks

Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + immediate artifact asks (security gating)

Thanks Dylan — good summary. Couple clarifications from our side:

1) We will need a BAA for any solution that processes PHI. Our legal prefers Dedicated + customer-managed KMS, but we are open to Private VPC if the deployment timeline works.
2) SOC2: we'll run vendor intake against Redwood's SOC2. Please confirm the audit period covered in your attached report and whether you can provide a control matrix mapping (we'll need mapping to CC6, CC7 controls).
3) Network: we will send a network diagram and allowed egress list.
4) KMS: preference is for BYOK with HSM-backed keys; account-level managed keys are only acceptable if we have a contractual guarantee and key rotation visibility.

Can Marissa and Karthik join a technical call on Wednesday 30th at 10am PT? If so, we'll send calendar invite and include our infrastructure security engineer (Aaron Li).

Also: are there any size/throughput SLAs for Dedicated that affect cost significantly? Our procurement wants a ballpark for committed throughput vs burst.

Regards,
Aisha

--
Aisha Khan
Head of IT Security, Medisure Health
aisha.khan@medisure.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + immediate artifact asks (security gating)

Aisha — great, thanks for the clarity. Quick answers and commitments:

SOC2: The attached SOC2 Type II covers Jan–Dec 2025. I’ll also add a control-mapping worksheet for CC6/CC7 by Monday; that should expedite your vendor intake.

KMS: We support BYOK with customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private flows. For Hosted API we only offer managed keys; we can provide detailed key-handling docs but BYOK is not available on the public shared endpoint.

Dedicated capacity SLAs / throughput:
- Baseline: you pick a reservation size (e.g., X tokens/sec) with predictable cost.
- Burst: configurable burst pool (short-duration) that you can enable during peaks.
- Pricing impact: committed baseline is billed at discounted unit rates; burst is billed at higher incremental rate. I’ll surface a short pricing sketch in the follow-up so procurement has a ballpark.

Confirming Wed 30th 10am PT — Marissa, Karthik, Soojin and I will join. I’ll send a calendar invite and drop a draft agenda: network requirements, KMS integration, audit logs export, and an initial Dedicated capacity sizing exercise.

Attached: network diagram for our recommended Dedicated-VPC pattern (redwood-dedicated-vpc-network-diagram.pdf).

Action items (owner):
- Dylan: send calendar + draft pricing sketch + control-mapping worksheet (by Mon)
- Medisure: share SOC2 vendor intake form (or confirm checklist) + network diagram + KMS requirement
- Marissa/Karthik: prepare Dedicated/VPC deployment checklist and pilot timeline estimate

See you Wed —
Dylan

--

Team — forwarding the thread from Medisure. High-level ask: scope Dedicated + VPC with BYOK as the preferred path; Medisure will validate our SOC2 and wants control mapping.

Please prepare the following before Wed:
- Marissa: one-pager (max) that explains the Dedicated + VPC deployment flow, time-to-prod milestones, and what we need from the customer (network ACLs, subnets, peering details).
- Karthik: short checklist for BYOK integration (supported KMS vendors, rotation windows, HSM requirements).
- Soojin (Legal): redline guidance on the BAA template they sent and any standard carve-outs we should expect.

I added the SOC2 and BAA template we shared with Medisure. We'll also need a pricing sketch for a 12-month committed Dedicated baseline vs on-demand; I can draft the numbers but would like your input on staging assumptions.

If you think Private on-prem is preferable for being conservative with keys, call it out in the one-pager with estimated delta in lead time and cost.

Thanks — please push your drafts to the shared folder linked below by EOD Tue so I can consolidate.
